segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Christy Collard

, resident, thanked the Council for their efforts. She explained the sidewalks and crosswalks would be made safer around the Greenwood Elementary due to comments made at a previous meeting. The Mayor noted they would begin work on the cross walk this summer.

entities.speaker: Brian Blackhurst
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Brian Blackhurst

, resident, said he lived behind a short-term rental. He explained the people living there were disturbing and there was no one to call to enforce the ordinance. He said this was a problem and suggested imposing limitations on short-term rentals. He noted the people renting the homes did not live in American Fork and did not care about the disturbances they created.
View minutes, page 5

entities.speaker: Cheryl Kite
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Cheryl Kite

, resident, commented she was retiring from Oklahoma. She said it was unfair the neighbors were turning their homes into hotels. She explained she did not know them, and it was not safe. She said she was concerned about the traffic and the children. She suggested they restrict where Air B&B are allowed in the City.

Council Member Christiansen asked where she suggested to put the Air B&Bs. Ms. Kite responded St. George and other cities had made restrictions and they should investigate what they had done.
View minutes, page 5

entities.speaker: Jerry Edwards
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Jerry Edwards

, resident, said he agreed with the previous speakers. He said he was in favor of the ordinance. He suggested they create more restrictions to the ordinance in the future. He noted there were some residents that abided by the rules and did not deserve to be punished. He commented there had been issues with parking and this needed to be addressed. He said they should consider the property owner’s rights to rent their property.

Council Member Carroll asked if he would prefer no short-term rentals. Mr. Edwards responded he thought the ordinance was a compromise. He thought there should be areas where short-term rentals were not allowed.

Council Member Shelton commented he thought Mr. Edwards did not want the rentals in his area. Mr. Edwards commented he thought the ordinance was partially what they wanted but they needed to make more restrictions.
View minutes, page 5

entities.speaker: Jerry Kite
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Jerry Kite

, resident, commented he agreed with Ms. Kite. He explained Provo restricts Air B&B only where hotels were present. He suggested excluding R1 zoning from short-term rentals. He said this was the zoning they wanted because it was a safe community. He explained their neighbors had rented out their homes and their street had become a hotel. He said this was a threat to his family because of the type of people that used the properties. He shared a story where a woman was kidnapped by people that rented an Airbnb.
View minutes, page 5

entities.speaker: John Woffinden
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
John Woffinden

, of the Planning Commission, commented that he voted against this ordinance. This was the worst ordinance he had seen. He thought it would contaminate residential areas. He noted there were several homes in his neighborhood that had illegal apartments and this ordinance would only make things worse. He said that enforcement was extremely difficult.
View minutes, page 5

entities.speaker: Julie Bleazard
entities.comment-context: Public hearing on short-term rental ordinance

segments.text: May 14, 2019 — As recorded in the meeting minutes:
Julie Bleazard

, resident, commented she had lived in American Fork for six years. She said she loved her neighborhood but did not like the short-term rentals. She said this scared her because she did not know who was living in these homes. She thanked the Council for investigating this issue. She noted she understood why people needed to rent out their homes. She said it was good they were making an ordinance so the police could act on problems.

asked if it was illegal to have an Airbnb in American Fork. Mr. Merrill responded in the negative. He cited the City code and noted it was ambiguous on the topic. Mr. Blackhurst commented tabling the issue would allow this problem to continue for another year.
